taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 26, Cheilanthes siliquosa: fronds many, crowded, 7-30 cm. long.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 26, Cheilanthes siliquosa: fronds 7-30 cm. long.

traits.life_span.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 26, Cheilanthes siliquosa: rhizome multicipital, cespitose.

traits.woodiness.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 26, Cheilanthes siliquosa: a fern.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Hoshizaki and Moran, Fern Grower's Manual (2001) p. 193, Aspidotis densa: evergreen.

traits.reproduction.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 26, Cheilanthes siliquosa: sporangia of adjacent sori crowded in a continuous line.

traits.rosette.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 26, Cheilanthes siliquosa: fronds many, crowded.

traits.perennation.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 26, Cheilanthes siliquosa: rhizome multicipital, the divisions oblique.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Hoshizaki and Moran, Fern Grower's Manual (2001) p. 193, Aspidotis densa: rhizome short-creeping to ascending, branching, fairly compact.

traits.leaf_posture.note: Fronds stiffly erect in a dense tuft, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 33941332, 244171741, 33941322, 33941329, 244000992, 29003607, 33941319, 155550924): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 26, Cheilanthes siliquosa: blades broadly ovate, deltoid-oblong, or subpentagonal, 1.5-8 cm. long.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 26, Cheilanthes siliquosa: stipes 5-22 cm. long, nearly naked.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: blades 1.5 cm to 7 cm broad, about as broad as long, as in the photos.

traits.leaf_division.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 26, Cheilanthes siliquosa: blades 3-pinnate below.

traits.division_pattern.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 26, Cheilanthes siliquosa: pinnae few, close, oblique.

traits.division_order.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 26, Cheilanthes siliquosa: blades 3-pinnate below.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 26, Cheilanthes siliquosa: blades broadly ovate, deltoid-oblong, or subpentagonal.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 26, Cheilanthes siliquosa: segments narrowly linear, mucronate, their margins sharply revolute.

traits.stipe_colour.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 26, Cheilanthes siliquosa: stipes brownish-castaneous, lustrous; sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.stipe_scales.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 26, Cheilanthes siliquosa: stipes nearly naked.

traits.stipe_scale_extent.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 26, Cheilanthes siliquosa: stipes nearly naked, the rhizome's scales at their foot.

traits.sorus_position.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 26, Cheilanthes siliquosa: margins sharply revolute, the sporangia in a continuous line.

traits.indusium.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 26, Cheilanthes siliquosa: margins revolute, giving rise to a continuous delicate erose-denticulate indusium.

traits.frond_dimorphism.note: Hoshizaki and Moran, Fern Grower's Manual (2001) p. 193, Aspidotis densa: hemidimorphic; fertile fronds with longer stipes and narrower segments.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a dense tuft of stiff, wiry brown stalks, each with a small triangular blade divided into many narrow linear segments.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for Indian's dream from its sources and the photos the traits cite; the rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.15 m tall at 4 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.
